lineage_context.teaching_goal: Teach the project ocotillo through petiolar spines, rain-triggered short-shoot leaf fascicles, red tubular flowers with many exserted stamens, and a 3-valved capsule with fringed-winged seeds.

project_scope.note: The project has a single Fouquieriaceae taxon. Kew recognizes Fouquieriaceae as sister to Polemoniaceae within Ericales, making this an especially useful morphology contrast.

family_diagnostics.where_to_look_first: Start at a spine: the long-shoot leaf petiole persists and hardens into a spine, while clusters of short-lived leaves arise on short shoots at its base after rain.
family_diagnostics.vegetative: Spiny woody xerophyte; long-shoot leaves are associated with petiolar spines, and drought-deciduous secondary leaves appear in fascicles on short shoots.
family_diagnostics.reproductive: Terminal panicles of showy tubular 5-lobed flowers; 10–16 or more stamens, often exserted; superior 3-carpellate ovary.
family_diagnostics.fruit: 3-valved loculicidal capsule with flattened seeds fringed by dense hairs that form a wing.
family_diagnostics.field_tip: Petiolar spine + rain-responsive leaf fascicle + red tube + many exserted stamens is a nearly unforgettable family package.

visual_lesson.teaching_order: petiolar spine → short-shoot leaf fascicle → red tubular flower → many stamens → 3-valved capsule/winged seed
visual_lesson.intro: Ocotillo gives us one of the best morphology stories in the learner: a leaf stalk becomes a spine, then new leaves repeatedly flush from short shoots beside it after rain.

steps.title: 1 · Show how the spine is made
steps.look_for: Persistent leaf-petiole base hardening into a conical spine.
steps.why_it_matters: Explains the architecture instead of merely labeling the plant 'thorny.'

steps.title: 2 · Find the rain leaves
steps.look_for: Clusters of small drought-deciduous leaves emerging at the base of the spine.
steps.why_it_matters: One of the most visually memorable xerophyte adaptations in the project.

steps.title: 3 · Read the red tube
steps.look_for: Five-lobed tubular red-orange corolla in a dense terminal panicle.
steps.why_it_matters: Connects ocotillo to its Ericales reproductive architecture.

steps.title: 4 · Count many stamens
steps.look_for: Roughly 10–16 or more stamens extending from the corolla, not the 5 seen in Polemoniaceae.
steps.why_it_matters: Excellent tie-breaker from its close Polemoniaceae relative.

steps.title: 5 · Finish with capsule and fringed seed
steps.look_for: Three-valved capsule and flat seeds edged by dense hairlike wings.

comparisons.title: Fouquieriaceae vs Polemoniaceae
comparisons.rule: Both are close Ericales relatives with fused tubular flowers and superior ovaries. Fouquieriaceae is woody/spiny with 10–16+ stamens and fringed-winged seeds; Polemoniaceae project plants are herbs with 5 stamens and 3-valved capsules.

comparisons.title: Ocotillo vs cactus
comparisons.rule: Ocotillo has true leaves that repeatedly flush after rain and petiolar spines; cacti are identified by areoles. Do not teach ocotillo as a cactus.

visual_lesson.caveat: Fouquieria splendens is native to southwestern Texas, but family recognition here is independent of strict Hays County nativity.

genera.fast_cue: petiolar spines + rain-flushed leaf fascicles + red tubular flower + many stamens

taxonomy_reconciliation.note: Accepted; native range extends to southwestern Texas.

visual_targets.annotation_goal: label leaf blade, petiole and persistent spine

count/label stamen set against corolla tube
